Recalling the state of the country when the APC took over, Kana said, “Our party came in 2015 and met the country in total disarray.” The Minister of Defence and First Secretary of the directorate, General Christopher Musa, said Tinubu’s return was not in doubt and that the task now was to secure the ground for it. “The return of Mr President is not an issue that we should even start worrying about, because God’s willing, he is coming back. The task before us now is to provide the enabling environment for it to happen. The issue of security is paramount and is key to our success. “We must do everything possible to make sure that Nigeria is safe and secure. And our campaigns are peaceful and safe, because I think that is the most critical aspect of what we do,” he said. The Director of Intelligence and Security of the Council, Major General Sarkin Yaki Bello (retd), who inaugurated the structures, said its members must work within the law. “Our duty is to protect Mr President and the people, and not to threaten them, to preserve order, not to create fear, and to support a peaceful democratic process,” he said. He told members what the stakes were. “What is at stake, gentlemen, is the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for a second term in office,” Sarkin Yaki said. The Special Adviser to the President on Homeland Security, Major General Adeyinka A. Famadewa (retd), said the directorate’s job was to keep the process orderly. “Without security, what you have is chaos, and chaos is not what we need at this time. And our job is to make the process safe and secure,” he said. Former Chief of Defence Staff and Chairman, Operations and Field Coordination of the directorate, General Abayomi Gabriel Olonisakin (retd), said work would start immediately. “The job is just starting. By this weekend, the flag-off will start, and we are expected to go to the 36 states,” he said. Speaking for the inaugurated officers, the Southwest coordinator of the directorate, Lt. Gen. item.title: At Strasbourg, Gio Reyna is starting to gain what had been elusive: momentum
item.description: A goal against PSG is proof on the scoresheet of what can be seen on the teamsheet: At long last, Reyna is getting consistent minutes. For an entire four-year cycle, to write about Gio Reyna was to write about his potential – especially the nagging feeling that it was going unfulfilled. Once hyped as possibly the greatest prospect in US men’s history, a series of injuries kept him from simply taking the field, much less making his mark on it. Since his emergent 2020-21 season, when he logged nearly 2,000 Bundesliga minutes running alongside Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, and Jadon Sancho, Reyna finished each of the ensuing five seasons without even cresting 630 league minutes. “Rotational” became a generous descriptor for his role at Nottingham Forest on loan, and then last season with Borussia Mönchengladbach. Still, Gregg Berhalter and Mauricio Pochettino kept involving Reyna with the US squad based on that pesky potential – betting that, on his day, he still had the raw talent to do what few compatriots could. Continue reading...

item.title: 9 Years Later, The Simpsons' Controversial Character Officially Returns
item.description: In January 2020, Hank Azaria stepped down from voicing one of the most iconic characters on The Simpsons , Kwik-E-Mart owner Apu Nahasapeemapetilon. The actor and the show's writers agreed that the portrayal of Apu was charged with racial stereotypes, and they apologized while the character and his family were quietly moved to the background of the show. On Oct. 18, 2026, in the season 38 episode "The Revengening," Apu officially returned to The Simpsons with a new voice actor.

item.title: AI’s epic cash call is matched only by its ability to strangle revenue streams
item.description: As it was written, so it has come to pass. A while back, we suggested that given how good AI was at code analysis, it would become possible to clone large applications. And then where would we be? Here, that’s where. An industrious individual has released source code and binaries for Claude-copied Microsoft Office and Adobe Creative Suite programs, disappointingly not calling elements of the latter Fauxtoshop. They’re in pre-alpha states of incomplete bugginess, but with substantial functionality, which is proof of how insanely productive AI can be given a task needing zero creativity and wearing "This is what a proof of concept looks like" and "Unintended Consquesences" T-shirts. They could also add Karma Police to their wardrobe. It’s clear that Microsoft and Adobe are facing some competition from what their rival describes as "clean-room reimplementations." It’s also unclear that there is any law against it. You can’t copyright functionality, the code has been generated in Rust with claimed clean-room conditions, and while there may be something in claiming that the works are substantially derivative, there’s a big problem here. Companies that sell AI trained on the biggest theft of IP in history are going to need unmatched legal dexterity to claim that AI shouldn’t be allowed to sully their own IP. Chutzpah used to be defined as a child on trial for murdering their parents begging for mercy on the grounds that they’re an orphan. We’ll have to update that. The post-codeclone world is going to be interesting. Everything becomes effectively open source, which closes down substantial revenue streams for big companies who had assumed lock-in. The motivation to build ab-initio alternatives may go away, in open source as well as closed. The push to subscription-only cloud-hosted products, where nobody can get their thieving AI prompts on binaries, seems an obvious counter move, but AI can control and scrape a web interface, which is all it needs. It's an arms race that won’t be won by humans. Code cloning is just the latest case of AI being so disruptive it threatens its creators. Another is the doom loop that Microsoft-OpenAI acknowledged in internal emails: by siphoning away the ad revenue that pays for content, AI chokes off the data it depends on. It's deforestation by companies that built their business on other people's IP. The biggest potential point of failure is the money. How revenues will hold up against cheaper or free Chinese models is a concern, given the high importance assigned by Beijing to develop AI as a global influence vector. The models themselves are very efficient, in part because of export regulations on high-end silicon and something of a glut of older datacenters. This wouldn’t be the first time restricting access to technology is an evolutionary driver with a poor outcome for those doing the restricting. A much bigger issue is: where will the money come from to build the infrastructure that is needed to support the claims
item.content:encoded: As it was written, so it has come to pass. A while back, we suggested that given how good AI was at code analysis, it would become possible to clone large applications. And then where would we be? Here, that’s where. An industrious individual has released source code and binaries for Claude-copied Microsoft Office and Adobe Creative Suite programs, disappointingly not calling elements of the latter Fauxtoshop. They’re in pre-alpha states of incomplete bugginess, but with substantial functionality, which is proof of how insanely productive AI can be given a task needing zero creativity and wearing "This is what a proof of concept looks like" and "Unintended Consquesences" T-shirts. They could also add Karma Police to their wardrobe. It’s clear that Microsoft and Adobe are facing some competition from what their rival describes as "clean-room reimplementations." It’s also unclear that there is any law against it. You can’t copyright functionality, the code has been generated in Rust with claimed clean-room conditions, and while there may be something in claiming that the works are substantially derivative, there’s a big problem here. Companies that sell AI trained on the biggest theft of IP in history are going to need unmatched legal dexterity to claim that AI shouldn’t be allowed to sully their own IP. Chutzpah used to be defined as a child on trial for murdering their parents begging for mercy on the grounds that they’re an orphan. We’ll have to update that. The post-codeclone world is going to be interesting. Everything becomes effectively open source, which closes down substantial revenue streams for big companies who had assumed lock-in. The motivation to build ab-initio alternatives may go away, in open source as well as closed. The push to subscription-only cloud-hosted products, where nobody can get their thieving AI prompts on binaries, seems an obvious counter move, but AI can control and scrape a web interface, which is all it needs. It's an arms race that won’t be won by humans. Code cloning is just the latest case of AI being so disruptive it threatens its creators. Another is the doom loop that Microsoft-OpenAI acknowledged in internal emails: by siphoning away the ad revenue that pays for content, AI chokes off the data it depends on. It's deforestation by companies that built their business on other people's IP. The biggest potential point of failure is the money. How revenues will hold up against cheaper or free Chinese models is a concern, given the high importance assigned by Beijing to develop AI as a global influence vector. The models themselves are very efficient, in part because of export regulations on high-end silicon and something of a glut of older datacenters. This wouldn’t be the first time restricting access to technology is an evolutionary driver with a poor outcome for those doing the restricting. A much bigger issue is: where will the money come from to build the infrastructure that is needed to support the claims AI is using to justify its growth. Gartner says that there’s not enough return on investment to drive that growth, while a much more engaging SemiAnalysis podcast predicts total capex by 2030 of $11 trillion and asks where it’s going to come from. If you’re interested in understanding AI and aren't following SemiAnalysis, you’re not interested in understanding AI, and while the outfit is relentlessly optimistic it’s also wildly well-informed. In this case, the structure of the investment market for AI is picked apart. It is very weird. Neocloud is made up of startups with a voracious appetite for cash, but no investment grade status. Thus, Nvidia backstops them, guaranteeing to rent unsold capacity for a fixed price for long enough to guarantee enough revenue to attract other investment. Other cash-rich big tech companies do similar things. This backstopping, also known more wryly as "balance sheet as a service," effectively shifts more risk to investment-rated companies. It's an increasingly important capex enabler, but as SemiAnalysis says, it’s necessarily limited, especially if AI itself has blown a hole in the enterprise. Or take the residual value of the older compute. Normally, the book value and revenue capabilities of datacenter chips depreciates over five years or so to some nominal value. That’s not happening here, where chips of that vintage are suddenly producing the same or more revenue than they did when they were new. Such are the peculiarities of a supply-constrained market used to rapid obsolescence. Surely a good thing, though? No. It’s another strange and hard-to-model factor in a market defined by strange and hard-to-model factors. Don’t even mention AGI. Or models too dangerous to use. Or model collapse. Many investors do not like the strange and hard to model, including huge pools of institutional funds. There are models that can blend in risk-averse investors to speculative investments, but those who remember the clever models that blew up the global economy nearly twenty years ago are not yet all dead. The tl;dr of the answer to where do you get enough money to make AI work as promised, is: nobody knows. What happens if the capex has no cap to ex? See previous answer. It may be an infantile affliction to have animation clips come to mind when considering AI, but it can’t be helped. Agentic AI? Mickey Mouse as the sorcerer's apprentice in Fantasia. Big Tech pushing out AI as fast as it can? Wile E Coyote sawing through the branch he’s sitting on. AI investment market? Any of Caine’s quests in the Amazing Digital Circus. We’re all along for the ride, whether we like it or not. ®

item.title: UN Agency Slashes Gaza Food Aid Over Funding
item.description: The World Food Programme has said it will end monthly assistance to 500,000 people in Gaza due to a funding shortfall, despite acute needs in the war-battered Palestinian territory. With the cutbacks, 1.1 million Palestinians in Gaza — still about half the population — will be receiving either food or cash assistance each month from the UN agency, in reduced amounts. Palestinians arrive at to collect a food ration box provided by the World Food Programme (WFP), at a distribution centre in the village of Al-Zawayda, in the centre of the Gaza Strip on October 27, 2025. Photo by BASHAR TALEB / AFP The World Food Programme said on Monday that its efforts had mitigated the effects during a famine last year in Gaza — a description of the situation disputed by Israel — and warned that conditions had not improved to the point that it can take away aid. “People are not safe. Airstrikes continue on a daily basis. People continue to be displaced,” Shaun Hughes, the WFP country director, told AFP at the agency’s office in east Jerusalem. “Almost everybody remains without a permanent home to live in. And the humanitarian conditions are brutal,” he said. According to the latest assessments, 1.4 million people — or two-thirds of Gaza’s population — are still “acutely food insecure” and need humanitarian assistance to survive, he said. In August last year, the UN’s Integrated Food Security Phase Classification said that Gaza was suffering famine conditions. Israel, which has blockaded the territory and attacked it relentlessly since the unprecedented October 7, 2023 attack on it by Hamas, described the finding as a lie. The famine classification was lifted in December, two months after a US-brokered ceasefire was announced in Gaza. Israel has kept striking Gaza since then, vowing to kill anyone involved in the October 7 attack. Since the ceasefire, the WFP has been able to step up assistance and has been reaching between 1.5 million and 1.8 million people every month. “This has been a lifeline. But now, rather than being able to sustain and scale up that assistance, we’re actually having to reduce it,” Hughes said. “And that’s not because we don’t have humanitarian access to deliver food; that’s because we don’t have funding.” Less Aid To Each Recipient In addition to reducing the number of people who receive rations, the WFP has been forced to shrink the content. Families receiving food assistance will now get only one food parcel instead of two and a smaller bag of wheat flour, the WFP said in an operational note. The 75,000 families who receive assistance in cash will see the amount reduced from 1,250 to 750 shekels ($400 to $240) per month. The WFP is funded by governments as well as private donors. It has seen a sharp drop in resources, including after President Donald Trump returned to power in the United States and drastically slashed contributions to UN agencies as well as bilateral aid. The agency says it needs about $450 million over the next six month

Since the ceasefire, the WFP has been able to step up assistance and has been reaching between 1.5 million and 1.8 million people every month. “This has been a lifeline. Families receiving food assistance will now get only one food parcel instead of two and a smaller bag of wheat flour, the WFP said in an operational note. The 75,000 families who receive assistance in cash will see the amount reduced from 1,250 to 750 shekels ($400 to $240) per month. The WFP is funded by governments as well as private donors. It has seen a sharp drop in resources, including after President Donald Trump returned to power in the United States and drastically slashed contributions to UN agencies as well as bilateral aid. The agency says it needs about $450 million over the next six months for its operations in Gaza and the West Bank, but in 2026 it has only received about half the usual financing for the Palestinian territories. In September, the agency also reduced by half the number of aid recipients in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967, from 400,000 to 200,000. “Now is not the time in the history of Palestine and Gaza to turn away from what is happening in Gaza,” Hughes said. The WFP says that conditions have moderately improved in Gaza but noted that needs could rise again with the onset of winter. Israel has allowed more goods into Gaza under the terms of the Trump ceasefire but still imposes heavy restrictions, turning away shipments of anything that is seen as having potential military use — a policy that has included blocking even prosthetic limbs, according to the United Nations. Israel has ramped up longstanding criticism of the United Nations since the Gaza war, accusing the world body of bias and perpetuating dependency among Palestinians. item.title: African players in Europe: Mbeumo goal eases pressure on Carrick
item.description: Cameroon star Bryan Mbeumo scored his fourth Premier League goal this season for struggling Manchester United in a 1-1 away draw against Leeds United at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND BRYAN MBEUMO (Manchester United) Mbeumo netted to ensure under-fire United boss Michael Carrick did not suffer another damaging defeat. Mbeumo put United ahead in the 35th minute against bitter rivals Leeds at Elland Road as he slotted home a Youri Tielemans cross. Leeds hit back to rescue a draw thanks to Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s second-half goal, but avoiding defeat was vital for Carrick after United’s poor start to the season. ALEX IWOBI (Fulham) The Nigeria midfielder’s first goal since March clinched a maiden Premier League win for Cottagers boss Alvaro Arbeloa. Iwobi netted in the 33rd minute of the 1-0 win against Hull at Craven Cottage, taking Sander Berge’s pass and hitting a low strike that squirmed under Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis. That was enough to lift Fulham out of the relegation zone and give former Real Madrid manager Arbeloa some much-needed breathing space. SPAIN EZ ABDE (Real Betis) Morocco international Abde scored against his former side Barcelona in Real Betis’s pulsating 5-2 La Liga defeat. The 24-year-old winger produced a sharp finish early in the second half for his fourth goal in his last five matches for the Andalucian side. BIL NSONGO (Deportivo La Coruna) Deportivo La Coruna striker Nsongo netted his first goal of the season to secure the Galician outfit a point against Levante in a 1-1 draw. The 22-year-old Cameroon international reacted quickest to reach a rebound in the box and bundle the ball home. ITALY AKOR ADAMS (Venezia) Nigerian Adams scored as bottom club Venezia ended a six-match losing steak since the Serie A season began by defeating former champions Napoli 1-0. New Venezia head coach Davide Nicola made a dream debut as Adams latched on to a long ball and scored with a deflected strike after 49 minutes. ANGE-YOAN BONNY (Inter Milan) The Ivory Coast forward wrapped up a 3-1 win for defending champions Inter Milan away to Bologna by scoring six minutes from time. Bonny netted after being set up by fellow substitute and scorer Carlos Augusto. GERMANY IBRAHIM MAZA (Bayer Leverkusen) Leverkusen midfielder Maza continued his impressive development with a goal and an assist in a 2-1 Bundesliga home win over Freiburg. The Algerian turned in a Patrik Schick pass midway through the opening half and then created a goal for the Czech with an excellent dribble late in the game. Named man of the match, Maza said he was “building chemistry” with veteran striker Schick, the first Bayer player to score in the first six games of the season. The post African players in Europe: Mbeumo goal eases pressure on Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Four Soldiers Dead, Dozens Injured In Canada Military Base Fire
item.description: Four soldiers were killed, and dozens injured in a fire at a military base in Alberta province, one of the worst peacetime tragedies to hit Canada’s armed forces on home soil, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Sunday. Carney made the solemn announcement without providing details on what caused the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright on Saturday. “It is with deep sadness that I can confirm, at this time, that four service members have lost their lives and that their loved ones have been notified,” Carney said in the capital Ottawa, adding that “dozens of others have been seriously injured.” “This is one of the worst tragedies the Canadian Armed Forces have experienced on Canadian soil in peacetime,” he said. Additionally, 19 were critically injured, eight were stable, and 12 were ambulatory after being treated for injuries, officials told reporters at a news conference Sunday. According to the Department of National Defence, the fire broke out around 4:00 pm local time (2200 GMT) Saturday in the base’s training area. Major General Wade Rutland told reporters that during “an outdoor exercise on the Alberta prairie,” soldiers were caught off guard by the advancing flames. “Within 30 seconds to a minute, they saw no fire, and then there was a fire on top of them,” Rutland said. “The fire did originate within the training area and did cross established fire guards before being contained, in conjunction with municipal authorities,” Rutland said. Rutland said it would be “at least a month” before he expected investigators to determine a cause, but responded to a suggestion circulating online that a hydrocarbon pipeline could have been hit by a munition. “You may have heard reports of explosions. Certainly, we do not believe this to be as a result of any oil and gas infrastructure, nor any outside interference,” Rutland said, adding that initial inspections indicated no damage to gas and oil infrastructure “but we will definitely check.” The Municipal District of Wainwright posted on social media that the fire had “spread rapidly due to high winds.” “Military and civilian crews fought this fire throughout the night in some of the worst conditions imaginable, risking their lives to protect their fellow Canadians,” Carney said. According to the Department of National Defence, the fire broke out around 4:00 pm local time (2200 GMT) Saturday in the base’s training area. Rutland said it would be “at least a month” before he expected investigators to determine a cause, but responded to a suggestion circulating online that a hydrocarbon pipeline could have been hit by a munition. “You may have heard reports of explosions. Certainly, we do not believe this to be as a result of any oil and gas infrastructure, nor any outside interference,” Rutland said, adding that initial inspections indicated no damage to gas and oil infrastructure “but we will definitely check.” The Municipal District of Wainwright posted on social media that the fire had “spread rapidly due to high winds.” “Military and civilian crews fought this fire throughout the night in some of the worst conditions imaginable, risking their lives to protect their fellow Canadians,” Carney said. Firefighters and emergency services close to Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Wainwright, Alberta, Canada, on October 18, 2026…photo by AFP ‘Every Step’ The Wainwright base is one of the largest bases operated by the Canadian Armed Forces, and it regularly hosts training exercises involving military personnel from NATO countries. Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, chair of NATO’s Atlantic alliance military committee, posted to X extending “deepest condolences” to those who lost family and wishing a “full recovery to all the injured.” “Wainwright is where Canadian soldiers, and so many Allies with them, train for the hardest tasks of our profession,” Cavo Dragone said, adding that “all 32 Allied Chiefs of Defence stand with you and the Canadian Armed Forces.” In the immediate aftermath of the incident, Warren Thirsk, a doctor at a hospital in the city of Edmonton, about 200 kilometers (110 miles) northwest of the base, told public broadcaster CBC that Wainwright’s health care facilities were “completely overwhelmed” by the number of patients requiring care. “We will care for the injured through every step of their recovery,” Carney said. “And we will stand by the women and men of our armed forces as they bear the weight of this loss, they will not carry it alone because in Canada we take care of one another.” The fire disrupted advance voting ahead of Monday’s vote on whether to begin the process toward a future referendum on Alberta’s independence from Canada. Alberta’s office responsible for overseeing provincial elections said the advance voting station in Wainwright had closed. item.title: Tom Cruise's 10/10 War Action Epic Is About to Say Goodbye to HBO Max
item.description: Tom Cruise has built a career out of playing larger-than-life characters, but some of his best performances are when he delves into the more vulnerable people beneath the movie-star bravado. Days of Thunder filters the story of a hotshot NASCAR driver through the humbling process of learning to trust someone, while Jerry Maguire finds a sports agent in the throes of learning that success means little without genuine human connection. Even Tropic Thunder , for all its outrageous comedy, gives Cruise room to disappear into a grotesque Hollywood executive whose insecurities are as ridiculous as his explosive temper. And Alejandro González Iñárritu’s Digger gives Cruise one of his most fascinating character studies yet as an oil tycoon with a brazen plan to save the world.

item.title: AI inference is running into a memory bottleneck. Huawei wants to tackle it with OceanStor M900
item.description: As organizations move from straightforward AI interactions towards longer conversations, complex reasoning and autonomous agents, the demands on their infrastructure are changing. Processing increasingly large amounts of context places significant pressure on memory capacity, while keeping accelerators supplied with data becomes just as important as raw computing power. One particular challenge is the key-value (KV) cache, which stores information generated during inference so models can reuse previous computations rather than repeatedly processing the same context. As context windows expand and multi-turn interactions become more demanding, these caches grow considerably. GPU memory and system memory provide fast access but are expensive and capacity constrained. Traditional storage offers greater capacity, yet its longer, CPU-mediated data paths can introduce latency that leaves valuable accelerator resources waiting for data. Huawei believes addressing this gap requires a different approach to storage. Bringing context memory closer to compute At HUAWEI CONNECT 2026 in Shanghai, Huawei introduced OceanStor M900 Context Memory Storage, designed to support AI inference across hyperscale datacenters and its Ascend SuperPoD infrastructure. The platform introduces what Huawei describes as a dedicated Context Memory Storage layer, extending KV cache beyond accelerator and system memory into a shared, multi-tier storage pool. Using Huawei's UnifiedBus high-speed interconnect, OceanStor M900 enables KV cache resources to be shared across a cluster, with Huawei claiming capacity of up to 64PB and substantially more context available per NPU. Its innovative ASU disk also integrates CPU, networking and storage controller functions. Combined with native KV semantics, this allows NPUs to access stored cache data in a single hop, avoiding conventional protocol conversion and CPU forwarding. According to Huawei, this approach reduces access latency to 60 microseconds, potentially doubling token throughput and halving time to first token in typical AI coding workloads. Cost and durability are also part of the proposition. Huawei's KV-aware adaptive storage technology manages data placement according to cache lifecycles, with claimed endurance of up to 24 drive writes per day, or 16 times that of conventional SSDs. The company argues this could reduce replacement and maintenance costs over time. The wider significance of OceanStor M900 lies in Huawei's approach to AI infrastructure. Rather than treating storage as a separate supporting component, the company is positioning memory, networking and compute as increasingly interconnected elements of inference performance. As agentic AI workloads grow, how efficiently infrastructure retains, shares and retrieves context may become as important as how quickly its accelerators can process it. Sponsored by Huawei

item.title: Police ‘Lost Control’ During Nationwide Protests In France, Says Interior Minister
item.description: French police “lost control” during nationwide protests marred by violence over the weekend, the interior minister admitted on Monday, with President Emmanuel Macron calling for a security review. Macron also refused Interior Minister Laurent Nunez’s resignation even as he acknowledged security and intelligence failures in the government response. Saturday’s demonstrations saw some half a million people turn out across France to protest the cost of living, but morphed into some of the worst violence to rock the country in years, with town halls and shops looted and set ablaze. People destroy the window of a Franprix store as clashes erupted at Place de la Republique following an unauthorised demonstration in central Paris on October 18, 2026, a day after nationwide protests against the “high cost of living”. More than 2,500 people were arrested, while almost 1,000 members of the security forces were injured. Injuries were also reported among protesters, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade. “On Saturday, in some major cities, you couldn’t look shopkeepers in the eye after hundreds of shops had been looted and tell them we hadn’t lost control,” Nunez said. Nunez acknowledged a “lack of anticipation” in the deployment of security forces on Saturday, whose numbers were insufficient to deal with the large crowds of rioters and looters on the fringes of the demonstrations. He estimated that the government had deployed some 60,000 law enforcement personnel across the country that day. “Given the damage that has been caused, it was only right that I should hand in my resignation,” Nunez said. The presidency said in a statement that Macron had rejected the resignation, however, citing “the necessity for continued leadership of law enforcement”. Instead, Macron ordered Nunez to “take all necessary steps to ensure transparency over the failures in planning and intelligence that led to the violence”. This photograph shows a television monitor broadcasting France’s President Emmanuel Macron giving a speech from the Elysee Presidential Palace the day after riots and looting on the sidelines of nationwide protests against the “high cost of living”, in Paris on October 18, 2026. Photo by LUDOVIC MARIN / AFP To end the “barricades and looting, he also requested that the interior minister promptly implement new operational methods for security forces to use on the ground in combating rioters,” the statement added. Looting continued on Sunday, with Paris Mayor Emmanuel Gregoire saying Monday that around 30 shops had been targeted in the capital the previous day, describing the scenes as “unbearable”. Nunez said some 350 people had been arrested in Paris on Sunday and overnight. Nationwide, police took more than 2,330 people into custody over the weekend, 70 per cent of whom were adults, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said Monday. More than 2,000 shops were expected to have been affected by the weekend’s violence across France,

More than 2,000 shops were expected to have been affected by the weekend’s violence across France, with damage running into “hundreds of millions of euros”, according to chamber of commerce president Alain Di Crescenzo. In an address to the nation Sunday evening, Macron slammed the “unbridled” violence and said local authorities would be able to ban — “if necessary” — certain rallies in coming days. But he stopped short of announcing drastic measures, such as a state of emergency or curfew. Saturday’s protests followed four weeks of high school student protests that at times also turned violent. item.title: 2027 not a replay of 2023 – Lagos APC tells Peter Obi
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has said presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, risks losing his political capital ahead of the 2027 general elections if he fails to demonstrate ideological consistency and organisational depth. APC spokesman in Lagos, Seye Oladejo, stated this on Monday, in a release, titled “2027: Peter Obi and the Expiration Date of Political Momentum.” Oladejo said Obi’s 2023 campaign tapped into public frustration, youth mobilisation and social media enthusiasm, describing it as a consequential moment in Nigeria’s democratic experience, but noted that riding a wave of public sentiment is different from possessing political depth and national structure. “Obi appears to have mistaken a moment of extraordinary political momentum for a permanent entitlement to electoral relevance. “Political capital, once accumulated, can depreciate when it is not reinforced by consistency, credible policies and sustained organisational development,” he said. Oladejo said Obi failed to convert the enthusiasm of 2023 into lasting political capital, arguing that social media visibility and rallies cannot substitute for effective national organisation and grassroots structures. “No two elections are the same. The 2023 phenomenon drew strength from a particular combination of public frustration and novelty. There is no guarantee these factors will reproduce in 2027,” he said. The Lagos APC spokesman faulted what he described as Obi’s political bed-hopping from the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Labour Party (LP) and subsequent realignments ahead of 2027, saying it raises questions about conviction. “Changing political parties is not inherently objectionable. The concern arises when repeated movement begins to create the impression that political platforms are interchangeable vehicles for personal ambition rather than institutions anchored in enduring principles,” Oladejo said. He also questioned Obi’s policy consistency, saying presidential leadership requires explaining costs, trade-offs and mechanisms for solving inflation, employment, debt and energy challenges. Oladejo criticised Obi’s recurring phrase “go and verify,” saying the invitation has sometimes exposed his claims to scrutiny that challenged their accuracy. “Verification is essential. The problem is that in numerous instances, the very invitation to verify has prompted scrutiny that has challenged the figures and assertions advanced,” he said. Oladejo said the Obidient movement must move from protest to policy and from mobilisation to organisation to become a durable national coalition. “The 2027 election will not be decided by who can most successfully recreate emotions of 2023. item.title: World Food Programme to end aid for half a million in Gaza due to funding shortfall
item.description: The UN World Food Programme has warned that funding shortages will leave about 500,000 people in the Gaza Strip without critical food aid in a territory where two thirds of the population remains acutely food insecure. The WFP said it is reducing its monthly assistance from 1.6 million to 1.1 million people.

item.title: Wike, Rivers lawmakers meet Fubara
item.description: By Davies Iheamnachor, Port Harcourt The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has led members of the Rivers State House of Assembly and local government chairmen in the state to a closed-door meeting with the Governor of the state, Siminalayi Fubara. The meeting, whose agenda has not been ascertained, was held at the primate residence of Fubara in Port Harcourt, Sunday evening. The high-profile meeting marked the first time Wike and the lawmakers visited the governor at his residence. The minister had led the delegation, comprising mainly members of the state assembly, led by its speaker, Rt Hon Martin Amaewhule, the candidate of the All Progressives Congress, Kingsley Chinda, and the state’s 23 local government chairmen, and other members of the Rainbow Coalition, to meet with the governor and his supporters. This was coming after an earlier meeting some weeks back in which Wike had also led members of the Rainbow Coalition in the state, including the candidate of the All Progressives Congress in the 2027 general elections, Kingsley Chinda, to meet with Fubara. It was, however, gathered that the Sunday meeting was in continuation of talks between the camps of Wike and Fubara in order to build on the ongoing reconciliation efforts in the state. It was gathered that the meeting was to strengthen efforts to put the political crisis that rocked the state behind and explore ways of accommodating Fubara’s loyalists in the new political setting of 2027. It was learned that at the end of the engagement, Wike and Fubara came out with smiles, likewise the lawmakers, LG Chairmen and other members of the Rainbow Coalition. At the entrance door where they took pictures, the speaker, Amaewhule, and others were captured in a video greeting and shaking hands with the governor, bowing and calling ‘Your Excellency’ even as Fubara acknowledged the greetings with smiles and later rejoined his political godfather, Wike, before all posed for the group photograph. It would be recalled that Fubara and the Amaewhule-led House of Assembly had been entangled in deep war since the political crisis that lasted for over two years following a protracted disagreement between Fubara and his predecessor, Wike. The lawmakers during the heat of the political crisis had on two different occasions attempted to impeach the governor before President Bola Tinubu intervened with the declaration of a state of emergency, suspending the governor and others. Following the disagreement and in spite of the seeming reconciliation, the minister, who is the political leader of the team, ruled out a second tenure stance for Fubara and handed the ticket of the party to Chinda. However, at the verge of the 2027 poll, Wike has resumed moving to bring back all the leaders of his team from the two camps back together. The post Wike, Rivers lawmakers meet Fubara appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Trump backs ally Netanyahu ahead of Israel’s tight election
item.description: US President Donald Trump endorsed on Sunday his ally Benjamin Netanyahu before Israel’s close-fought parliamentary election on October 27, providing a boost to the veteran prime minister’s bid to win a new mandate. Netanyahu touted his close relationship with the US president in a video released by his Likud party, saying that together they had “crushed Iran” and adding that re-election would allow him to work with Trump to “elminate the Iranian threat over the next two years, or even sooner”. The endorsement comes less than two weeks before Israel’s first vote since the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack, which opposition politicians have accused Netanyahu of bearing personal responsibility for after allegedly ignoring warnings. Trump and Netanyahu, who polls show is in a tight election race, have worked closely together on Israel’s multi-front wars after the Hamas-led attack, including bombarding Iran, and the endorsement could be a boon to his re-election campaign. “Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, using a common nickname for the Israeli leader. “This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much. Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel.” The election is seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, who quickly thanked the US leader for his support on Sunday. “Thank you, President Trump, for your tremendous support and for our work together. Together we will complete the mission!” he wrote on X. “I ask you to listen carefully to what President Trump said this evening,” Netanyahu told voters. “He said that together we have accomplished extraordinary things… But there is still a mission to complete.” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned Netanyahu was “driving America into another war”. “Last time you wanted to ‘finish the job’, Iran emerged even stronger. Want to try your luck again? Be our guest. But be careful; we have unfinished jobs too,” Araghchi wrote on X. Trump joined Netanyahu in a US-Israeli attack on Iran in late February but agreed to a ceasefire in April in the face of widespread US public opposition to the war, which had sent oil prices spiralling. Speaking at an event in August, Netanyahu said Trump “is our greatest friend, one of the greatest friends we have had in the White House”. item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump endorsed on Sunday his ally Benjamin Netanyahu before Israel’s close-fought parliamentary election on October 27, providing a boost to the veteran prime minister’s bid to win a new mandate. Netanyahu touted his close relationship with the US president in a video released by his Likud party, saying that together they had “crushed Iran” and adding that re-election would allow him to work with Trump to “elminate the Iranian threat over the next two years, or even sooner”. The endorsement comes less than two weeks before Israel’s first vote since the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack, which opposition politicians have accused Netanyahu of bearing personal responsibility for after allegedly ignoring warnings. Trump and Netanyahu, who polls show is in a tight election race, have worked closely together on Israel’s multi-front wars after the Hamas-led attack, including bombarding Iran, and the endorsement could be a boon to his re-election campaign. “Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, using a common nickname for the Israeli leader. “This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much. Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel.” The election is seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, who quickly thanked the US leader for his support on Sunday. “Thank you, President Trump, for your tremendous support and for our work together. Together we will complete the mission!” he wrote on X. “I ask you to listen carefully to what President Trump said this evening,” Netanyahu told voters. “He said that together we have accomplished extraordinary things… But there is still a mission to complete.” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned Netanyahu was “driving America into another war”. “Last time you wanted to ‘finish the job’, Iran emerged even stronger. Want to try your luck again? Be our guest. But be careful; we have unfinished jobs too,” Araghchi wrote on X. Trump joined Netanyahu in a US-Israeli attack on Iran in late February but agreed to a ceasefire in April in the face of widespread US public opposition to the war, which had sent oil prices spiralling. Speaking at an event in August, Netanyahu said Trump “is our greatest friend, one of the greatest friends we have had in the White House”. But relations between the two have at times been strained on Iran, with Netanyahu saying no diplomatic agreement was possible with Iran’s leadership, while Trump sought a negotiated end to the months-long conflict. – Voter warning – The endorsement comes after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned against a brewing “crisis” in the occupied West Bank after an American photojournalist for The Washington Post was injured in a brutal attack by Israeli settlers. “We’re very disturbed by those images and what we’re seeing,” Rubio told reporters Saturday. Netanyahu’s office said it was investigating the circumstances around the attack. With Israel and Netanyahu looking increasingly isolated on the world stage, Trump’s support is vital. Netanyahu, who turns 77 on October 21, is Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, having served on and off for more than 19 years. The wily political operator returned to power in December 2022, bringing in once-shunned ultra-nationalists and quickly tried to rein in the judiciary, which is examining corruption charges that could land him in jail. His main election rival is opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the centre-right Yashar party and a former military chief who regularly accuses Netanyahu of bearing personal responsibility for the October 7 attack. About seven million Israelis will be eligible to vote in the legislative election. Current polls show that neither Netanyahu’s bloc nor that led by Eisenkot is in a position to win the 61 seats needed to control the 120-seat parliament and form a governing coalition. Eisenkot said that only Israelis could choose who they want to run the country. Speaking at a conference in Tel Aviv, Eisenkot said he “admires” Trump “but Israel is a democratic country, only Israelis can choose their leaders”. But Trump warned against Israel electing “anyone other than Bibi”, writing that if voters chose one of his rivals, “America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so”. item.title: French student protests: 'There's been lack of investment in education for years now'
item.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Axel Berra-Vescio, French History-Geography and European section teacher in the Paris region. France's student protests are exposing what educators describe as years of structural neglect, widening educational inequalities and the cumulative consequences of controversial reforms. “We've been ignored basically about every demand we made,” Berra-Vescio says. He also condemns the police response to the demonstrations, warning that repression is unlikely to weaken a movement rooted in years of frustration over the future of public education.

item.title: 2027: Vote for candidate who’ll make your money buy more — Alaje advises Nigerians
item.description: Senior economist at SPM Professionals, Paul Alaje, has urged Nigerians to assess presidential candidates in the 2027 general election based on their ability to improve purchasing power, reduce living costs and make essential services more affordable. Alaje said voters should prioritise candidates whose economic policies would enable Nigerians to buy more with their earnings, rather than be swayed by promises of higher wages without corresponding improvements in real income. He made the remarks on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics while discussing the economic policies Nigerians should consider when evaluating candidates ahead of the 2027 presidential election. “Any candidate who is telling you that the money in your pocket will buy more, will improve more, and will afford your rent — that is the candidate you should vote for,” he said. The economist said an increase in nominal earnings would not necessarily translate into better living conditions if prices continued to rise faster than incomes. Explaining the concept of purchasing power, Alaje said Nigerians should consider what their earnings could buy and whether proposed economic policies would improve their ability to meet household needs. “You can earn more in naira terms. Like labour wants more money, you can. But will it buy more in real terms?” he asked. He said voters should examine candidates’ plans for making education more affordable, improving access to healthcare and addressing other pressures on household budgets. According to him, the central question should be which candidate can improve the real value of Nigerians’ earnings and make essential services accessible to more people. Alaje also warned that economic policies that fail to prioritise productivity could undermine the country’s economic performance. “Anybody who is not discussing productivity is going to run the economy down,” he said. He argued that productivity and other economic fundamentals must support reforms if they are to deliver sustainable improvements in living standards. 2027: Alaje urges Tinubu to address electricity The economist also called on President Bola Tinubu to take urgent steps to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, describing power supply as a critical factor in improving economic performance. “You need to do something urgent and critical about electricity,” he told the President. Alaje said countries that had successfully implemented reforms similar to Nigeria’s had underlying economic fundamentals that helped them achieve results. “Major economies that adopted the kind of reforms we are adopting and have results, they have fundamentals working for them,” he said. The post 2027: Vote for candidate who’ll make your money buy more — Alaje advises Nigerians appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PANDEF declares seven days of mourning for Dele Cole
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has declared seven days of mourning in honour of its leader and elder statesman, Patrick Dele Cole, who died in London at the age of 86. Cole, popularly known as Chief PDC, died weeks after celebrating his 86th birthday, leaving behind a legacy of service in journalism, education, diplomacy, public administration and politics. In a statement signed by PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, on behalf of the organisation’s Board of Trustees (BoT) and National Executive Committee (NEC), the forum described Cole’s death as a painful and irreplaceable loss. Igali said Cole played significant roles in the socio-cultural and political development of the Niger Delta, particularly in the formation and growth of PANDEF. The late Cole served as Editor-in-Chief of the Daily Times of Nigeria, one of the country’s leading national newspapers, and later as presidential adviser on foreign affairs. He also served as Nigeria’s ambassador to Brazil. According to Igali, Cole brought considerable intellectual depth and experience to various socio-cultural and socio-political organisations in the Niger Delta. PANDEF directed all its chapters in Nigeria and the diaspora to suspend official social activities for seven days, beginning October 18, 2026. It also directed that Cole’s photograph be displayed on its media platforms throughout the mourning period. Igali said Cole played a significant role in the region’s struggle for true federalism and resource control, noting that his commitment to the aspirations of the Niger Delta people remained firm even while he served as a special adviser in the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo. He added that Cole’s political choices were guided by his commitment to the interests and legitimate aspirations of the Niger Delta people. Cole’s political career included a presidential bid under the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and membership of the Board of Trustees of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), PANDEF said. The forum also acknowledged his contributions as a Christian leader and advocate of Nigeria’s cultural heritage, particularly the traditions and identities of the South-South region. Expressing condolences over his death, PANDEF extended its sympathies to his son, Rt. Hon. Tonye Cole, other members of the Cole family, the people of Abonnema in the Kalabari Kingdom, the Ijaw nation, the Rivers State Government and the people of Rivers State, as well as Nigerians across the country. The organisation urged the bereaved family and the wider Niger Delta community to draw comfort from the distinguished life and enduring contributions of the late elder statesman. PANDEF prayed for the peaceful repose of Cole’s soul. The post PANDEF declares seven days of mourning for Dele Cole appeared first on Vanguard News .

PANDEF prayed for the peaceful repose of Cole’s soul. The post PANDEF declares seven days of mourning for Dele Cole appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Farmers-herders violence in FCT
item.description: T hree people have been reportedly killed and several others injured in a renewed farmers-herders clash in Paikon-Kore community, Gwagwalada Area Council of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), with houses and a motorcycle reportedly set ablaze. The violence, which began on Saturday afternoon and continued until Sunday morning, also left several shops at the Paikon-Kore village market burnt and goods destroyed. Experts urge that there is a need to nip the brewing crisis in the bud to avoid recurring deadly scenarios witnessed in other states like Benue and Plateau states, where farmers-herders clashes have claimed hundreds of lives and displaced many. A resident of the community, Danlami Ibrahim, said the clash started after some herders allegedly allowed their cattle into a groundnut farm whose crops were yet to be harvested. According to him, one of the herders allegedly brought out a cutlass and attacked a farmer, severing one of his hands. Ibrahim said the incident sparked anger among residents, particularly after other community members learnt of the farmer’s injury, leading to a reprisal in which three herders were reportedly killed. He added that two houses, several shops and a motorcycle were set ablaze during the violence. The resident said the clash continued until Sunday morning, leaving several people injured. Some of the victims were subsequently taken to hospitals in Gwagwalada for treatment. A visit to the affected village market by our correspondent showed several wooden, zinc-built and container shops burnt, with smoke still billowing from some of the shops. At Sabon Nakowa Hospital, a private medical facility in Gwagwalada, some victims were seen receiving treatment. Two others were also observed undergoing treatment at the accident and emergency unit of the University of Abuja Teaching Hospital. The Secretary of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Gwagwalada Area Council chapter, Mohammed Usman, said three herders lost their lives. “For now, information at my disposal shows that three herders lost their lives. That is what I can say for now, while I am yet to get the number of those who sustained injuries,” he said. Usman said he would provide further information as it became available, adding that he had informed the Gwagwalada Area Council chairman, Kasim Mohammed Ikwa, about the incident. Ikwa, who visited the affected community on Sunday alongside the Divisional Police Officer, SP Aaron H. Kaura, and other security operatives, condemned the renewed violence, describing it as unfortunate. He said the council would convene a stakeholders’ meeting on Monday (today) to deliberate on the crisis and seek ways to prevent further violence. The chairman urged both warring parties to embrace peace and avoid actions capable of escalating tensions. He also called on youths in Paikon-Kore to exercise restraint and promote peaceful coexistence with other residents, warning against confrontation and retaliatory attacks. Ikwa advised farmers whose crops were damaged by cattle to report such incidents to the relevant security agencies rather than resorting to self-help. He noted that such conflicts often affected innocent people who might not even understand the circumstances that triggered the dispute. The chairman further urged residents to cooperate with security personnel deployed to the community, adding that an expanded security meeting had been convened, with youth leaders, the Sarkin Noma and other community leaders from both sides invited to seek a lasting solution. He said anyone who felt unfairly treated or believed their complaints had not received adequate attention should report directly to him for intervention, stressing that grievances must be addressed through lawful channels. Meanwhile, soldiers, police officers, vigilantes and personnel of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) have been deployed to the community to restore calm. The FCT Police Command spokesperson, SP Adeh Josephine, did not answer calls seeking the command’s reaction as of the time of filing this report. Not first clash Daily Trust recalls that the latest violence followed an earlier clash on August 11, 2026, across Paikon-Kore, Ibwa and Rafin-Zurfi communities, during which a farmer reportedly lost a hand and three other people sustained machete injuries. Following that incident, Ikwa summoned an emergency security meeting where traditional rulers, community leaders, village and district heads, Ardos of Fulanis, as well as representatives of various security agencies deliberated over the incessant farmers and herders clash. The chairman, at the end of the security meeting, set up a peace and investigative committee. He also carried out on-the-spot assessments of the three affected communities that witnessed cases of farmers and herders clashes. Ikwa promised that the committee’s report would be made public during the stakeholders meeting on Monday (today). Some residents, who spoke to our reporter, said the August 11 incident was a result of cows that allegedly strayed into a farm. They claimed that the tension heightened when the owner of the farm confronted the herders for allowing cows to graze inside his farm, a situation which they said led to a serious confrontation that left four persons injured. Ishaku Danjuma, a farmer, explained that a similar incident also happened in Paiko community on the same day, after some cows allegedly grazed inside a maize farm, resulting in clashes between farmers and herders in the community. He said the farmer queried the herders for allowing cows into the farm, which led to the clash. “If you make your investigations, you will discover that 95 per cent of incidents of farmers and herders clashes across the three communities were as a result of cows straying into people’s farms,” he said. A member of the Paiko community, Usman Yakubu, also said the incessant cases of farmers-herders clash were as a result of cows that allegedly invade farms to destroy crops in the rural communities in the area. He alleged that some herders allowed their cows to eat up some crops, a development he said led to serious confrontations between the affected farmers and the herders across the three communities. “It was as a result of the destruction of some crops which suddenly resulted in a confrontation between the affected farmers and herders, which later led to the injuring of four farmers across three villages,” he said. State of grazing reserves in Abuja The Paikon Kore Grazing Reserve in the Gwagwalada Area Council of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) is one of the gazetted reserves in Nigeria. The reserve sits on 9,500 hectares of land but most of the area has also been encroached upon by the communities around the area according to herders. In June 2022, a major crisis was averted when the then Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development, Dr Mohammad Mahmood Abubakar visited the reserve to flag off a pasture development programme when youth in the community and the herders started throwing stones at each other. Gbagyi farmers were opposed to the programme, and instead called for the place to be fenced, claiming that pasture development would attract large herdsmen and threaten farms around the reserve. Daily Trust reports that the grazing reserve at Kawu in the Bwari Area Council has not been effectively put into use due to a lack of basic facilities and infrastructure. The grazing reserve, which spans approximately 9,000 hectares, was originally designed to accommodate about 30,000 cattle and 10,000 households. item.title: Last moments of Shettima Muhammad Kashim
item.description: Architect Shettima Muhammad Kashim, son of the late Sir Kashim Ibrahim, the first indigenous governor of the defunct Northern Region, has died in a road accident in Abuja. Shettima, 67, reportedly died on Friday, October 16, hours after attending a book launch examining President Bola Tinubu’s administration. His remains were buried at Gudu Cemetery, Abuja on Saturday in accordance with Islamic rites after funeral prayers held at the National Mosque attended by dozens, including Vice President Kashim Shettima. Shettima Mohammed was said to have died after his car ran into a stationary truck in the Asokoro area of the Federal Capital Territory, sustaining fatal head injuries. Farmers-herders violence in FCT Rainbow coalition stirs more controversies in states His death came hours after he had met friends and associates at the Shehu Musa Yar’Adua Centre in Abuja for the launch of Tinubu: From Renewed Hope to Despair: A Critical Examination of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Government, edited by Professor Abubakar Siddique Mohammed of the Centre for Democratic Development and Research (CEDDERT), Zaria. Friends who were with him at the book launch described him as a humble, jovial and dependable person who maintained cordial relationships across political divides despite his family’s prominent place in Nigeria’s political history. Among those who paid tribute to him were Dr Garba Abari, former Director-General of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), and Professor Usman Yusuf, former Executive Secretary of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS). Abari said he spent several hours with the deceased on Friday before leaving for the Juma’at prayer, unaware that their meeting would be their last. “We were together with him, one other very close friend of his, Professor Usman Yusuf, and yet another friend of ours, Comrade Kalli Gazali,” Abari said. item.dc:creator: Dalhatu Liman
item.content:encoded: Architect Shettima Muhammad Kashim, son of the late Sir Kashim Ibrahim, the first indigenous governor of the defunct Northern Region, has died in a road accident in Abuja. Shettima, 67, reportedly died on Friday, October 16, hours after attending a book launch examining President Bola Tinubu’s administration. His remains were buried at Gudu Cemetery, Abuja on Saturday in accordance with Islamic rites after funeral prayers held at the National Mosque attended by dozens, including Vice President Kashim Shettima. Shettima Mohammed was said to have died after his car ran into a stationary truck in the Asokoro area of the Federal Capital Territory, sustaining fatal head injuries. Farmers-herders violence in FCT Rainbow coalition stirs more controversies in states His death came hours after he had met friends and associates at the Shehu Musa Yar’Adua Centre in Abuja for the launch of Tinubu: From Renewed Hope to Despair: A Critical Examination of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Government, edited by Professor Abubakar Siddique Mohammed of the Centre for Democratic Development and Research (CEDDERT), Zaria. Friends who were with him at the book launch described him as a humble, jovial and dependable person who maintained cordial relationships across political divides despite his family’s prominent place in Nigeria’s political history. Among those who paid tribute to him were Dr Garba Abari, former Director-General of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), and Professor Usman Yusuf, former Executive Secretary of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS). Abari said he spent several hours with the deceased on Friday before leaving for the Juma’at prayer, unaware that their meeting would be their last. “We were together with him, one other very close friend of his, Professor Usman Yusuf, and yet another friend of ours, Comrade Kalli Gazali,” Abari said. Mourners conveying the remains of late Alhaji Shettima Muhammad Kashim after funeral prayer at the National Mosque, Abuja on Saturday He said they had been together from about 10am until shortly after 1pm at the Yar’Adua Centre, where they exchanged banter and discussed matters in their usual friendly manner. Abari said he left the group for the Friday prayer at Banex Mosque, while Kashim and the others proceeded to Maitama Juma’at Mosque, popularly known as Yar’Adua Mosque. According to him, Kashim later took his friends home after the prayers and lunch before driving towards his residence in Asokoro, where the fatal accident occurred. Abari said the news of Kashim’s death was particularly shocking because the deceased was known to be an extremely careful driver. “One thing that is distinctive about him is that he is an extremely careful, cautious driver,” Abari said, adding that the same caution characterised the way Kashim approached his responsibilities. Describing him as a person who never flaunted his privileged family background, Abari said Kashim was well brought up, good-natured and friendly to people regardless of their social standing. “He was a personification of humility, never carrying any airs around him about the kind of family he came from,” he said. Abari added that although Kashim came from a political family and held his own political views, he never allowed political differences to damage his relationships with others. The former NOA director-general said the suddenness of the death was a reminder of the uncertainty of human life. “If I recall the moments we had together, I recall the banters, everything. He looked too far away from death. But we never knew that it was just hovering around,” he said. He prayed that Allah would forgive the deceased’s shortcomings and grant his family the strength to bear the loss. ‘We were friends for almost 50 years’ Yusuf, who said he had known Kashim for almost five decades, described him as a decent, dependable and God-fearing person. In his tribute, the former NHIS executive secretary said their friendship began at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, and endured for nearly 50 years. “Arch. Shettima Mohammed Kashim and I met in ABU Zaria and have been very good friends for almost 50 years,” he said. Recounting their final hours together, Yusuf said they attended the book launch at the Yar’Adua Centre on Friday and left the venue at about 1:20pm. He said they proceeded to a mosque in Wuse II for the Friday prayer before having lunch at a nearby restaurant. They later observed the Asr prayer at the mosque before Kashim dropped him at his residence at about 4:30pm. Yusuf said he received a call from Kashim’s son about half an hour later, informing him that the family had been told that his father’s car was involved in an accident in Asokoro and that the occupant had been taken to Asokoro General Hospital. He said he rushed to the hospital, where he met members of Kashim’s family and brothers, who informed him that the architect had died. According to Yusuf, Kashim’s car ran into a stationary truck, resulting in fatal injuries. “Shettima Mohammed Kashim was more than a friend to me and many. He was a good, decent, dependable and God-fearing person,” he said. “May Allah forgive all his shortcomings and reward him with Jannatul Firdaus,” he prayed. Career as an architect Despite his family’s political background, Kashim maintained a professional career in architecture and public service, according to Abari. He said the deceased was trained as an architect and remained committed to his profession rather than using his family connections to pursue a political career. Abari recalled that Kashim served as general manager of the Borno Housing Corporation in the 1980s before moving to the federal service, where he also worked with the Federal Housing Authority. His career, Abari said, reflected a commitment to the profession in which he was trained. “He did not abandon his training as an architect,” he said. Kashim was also known by the traditional title of Shettima of Borno, a title associated with his family’s longstanding place in the traditional and political history of the region. Yusuf said the title had a historical connection to his father, Sir Kashim Ibrahim, who was conferred with the title of Shettima of Borno in 1935 and later became Waziri of Borno in 1956. Sir Kashim Ibrahim served as the first indigenous governor of the Northern Region of Nigeria from 1962 to 1966. Although his father occupied a prominent position in the country’s political history, Abari said Kashim remained approachable and maintained friendships with people of different backgrounds and political persuasions. Kashim was married to a daughter of the late Alhaji Mai Deribe, a renowned businessman.

item.title: ADAMAWA FOR ASIWAJU!
item.description: The Microphone Has Been Tested. The Signal Is Strong. The Structure Is Ready. Adamawa is ready, and its message is clear: the political structure, leadership and grassroots network are firmly in place to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. With Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri providing leadership, direction and strategic coordination, the state is prepared to pursue a decisive victory. The commitment is firm, the objective is clear, and the target is 100% electoral victory across the board. Achieving this goal requires sustained engagement, unity of purpose and disciplined organisation. Every stakeholder, coordinator and supporter has a role to play in taking the message to the people and translating commitment into votes. At the centre of this mobilisation is the Adamawa Renewed Hope 226 Movement (ARH-226M), led by its Director-General, Professor Abdullahi Liman Tukur. It is a structured, coordinated, knowledge-driven and grassroots-focused political movement established to transform political support into organised electoral action. Its reach extends across every level of the state’s political landscape: * 4,104 Polling Units: Where every vote counts and community engagement must translate into electoral participation. * 226 Electoral Wards: Where grassroots mobilisation takes shape, relationships are strengthened and local priorities receive attention. * 21 Local Government Areas: Where leadership, coordination and stakeholder engagement connect the statewide mission with community action. Through its 21 experienced LGA coordinators, clear leadership structures and effective mobilisation strategies, ARH-226M is prepared to reach communities, engage stakeholders and consolidate support for the APC from the polling units to the state level. The task is to sustain a visible presence, listen to the people, communicate the Renewed Hope message clearly and encourage eligible voters to participate peacefully and confidently in the electoral process. From community meetings to stakeholder consultations, every engagement must strengthen trust, widen participation and reinforce a shared commitment to victory. With consistent follow-through and cooperation across party structures, the movement can keep its mobilisation focused and responsive to local realities. This coordinated effort will turn readiness into action, action into mobilisation and mobilisation into victory. Adamawa is ready. The structure is in place. The mission is achievable. One State. One Purpose. A Shared Commitment to Renewed Hope. With Fintiri as the leader, Adamawa will deliver, Insha Allah!

item.title: 'Quite horrifying': Afghan economic crisis leaves EU deportees with 'very little' to return to
item.description: Europe's increasingly pragmatic engagement with Afghanistan's Taliban rulers is exposing a fundamental contradiction between diplomatic non-recognition and political necessity. In an investigation for The New York Times, Pakistan and Afghanistan bureau chief Elian Peltier reveals how European governments are quietly expanding negotiations with the Taliban over migrant deportations, diplomatic representation and economic assistance. “Even though on paper European governments do not recognise the Taliban administration, in practice they meet much more frequently than most of us know,” Peltier explains.

item.title: Nigeria joins league of nations in global measurement pact
item.description: By Adaobi Abimbola Nigeria has joined the league of nations with globally recognised measurement standards following the signing of the Mutual Recognition Arrangement of the International Committee for Weights and Measures, CIPM MRA, in France. The agreement was signed by the Director-General of the Standards Organisation of Nigeria, SON, Dr Ifeanyi Chukwunonso Okeke, at the 28th General Conference on Weights and Measures CGPM. The signing coincided with the DG’s third anniversary in office. According to a statement made by SON’s Director of Corporate Affairs, Mrs. Ethan Talatu, Nigeria’s admission as an Associate State of the International Bureau of Weights and Measures, BIPM, took effect on June 4, 2026. The CIPM MRA is the framework through which national metrology institutes prove that their measurement standards are equivalent and earn global recognition for their calibration and measurement certificates. Okeke said that the arrangement would bring international recognition of Nigeria’s measurement capabilities, global acceptance of its calibration certificates and easier trade across borders. He added that it would reduce dependence on foreign metrology services, strengthen SON’s technical authority and open doors to scientific collaboration and capacity building. Nigeria now joins Egypt, Kenya, Morocco, South Africa and Tunisia as the only African countries with full BIPM membership. For manufacturers and small businesses, products can be tested locally and trusted abroad without the cost of foreign laboratories. The post Nigeria joins league of nations in global measurement pact appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG targets $7.1bn sugar investments, 110,000 jobs in 10 years
item.description: The Federal Government is targeting $7.1 billion in investments in the sugar industry over 10 years to boost domestic production above two million metric tonnes annually, create 110,000 jobs and save $2.1 billion in foreign exchange annually. The programme, coordinated by the National Sugar Development Council (NSDC), is aimed at reducing Nigeria’s dependence on imported raw sugar through increased sugarcane cultivation, processing capacity and private-sector investment. Executive Secretary of NSDC, Kamar Bakrin, disclosed the plan in Abuja, saying the initiative would strengthen local production and supporting agricultural infrastructure. Under the programme, the council is proposing 10 integrated sugar estates across Niger, Kwara, Oyo, Kaduna, Jigawa, Bauchi, Nasarawa and Adamawa states. The estates are expected to cover 143,478 hectares, with a combined milling capacity of 55,500 metric tonnes of sugarcane daily. According to NSDC, the proposed estates could produce 835,000 metric tonnes of sugar annually, while existing operators are expected to contribute another 1.22 million tonnes through increased output. The projects are also expected to support ethanol production and electricity generation, creating additional opportunities for agro-processing and value addition. To finance the programme, the council is seeking $5 billion in long-term debt and $2.1 billion in equity contributions from investors. Funding is expected to involve export credit agencies, development finance institutions and local financial organisations. NSDC also disclosed a $1 billion agreement with Chinese engineering company Sinomach, although the associated financing arrangements are yet to be completed. It is collaborating with the Bank of Industry on a proposed N10 billion Sugar Projects Acceleration Fund to support feasibility studies and prepare projects for investment. The post FG targets $7.1bn sugar investments, 110,000 jobs in 10 years appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Manufacturing index plunges 10% as cement sector contracts – NESG
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole Nigeria’s manufacturing business activity plunged by about 10 per cent in September 2026, as a contraction in the cement subsector and weakening performance across several industries dragged down the sector’s business index, the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) has said. The group’s Business Confidence Monitor (BCM) showed that the manufacturing Current Business Performance Index (CBPI) fell to 108.4 points in September from 120.4 points in August, amid persistent cost pressures, tight credit conditions and operational challenges. Despite the manufacturing setback, overall business activity maintained its expansionary momentum, with the composite CBPI rising to 117.8 points from 112.7 points in August and 107.9 points in September 2025. According to the NESG, expansion was recorded across all major sectors, with trade delivering the strongest performance. The sector’s index rose sharply to 128.5 points from 112.0 points in August. The manufacturing slowdown reflected mixed performances among the sector’s largest subsectors. Food, Beverage and Tobacco remained in expansion territory but recorded slower activity, while Textile, Apparel and Footwear performed more strongly than in the preceding month. Cement, however, moved into contraction. Business activity also contracted in Chemical and Pharmaceutical Products, Plastic and Rubber Products, Wood and Wood Products, Non-Metallic Products, Basic Metal, Iron and Steel, and Motor Vehicles and Assembly. Pulp, Paper and Paper Products remained in expansion, although its index was unchanged, while Electrical and Electronics recorded stronger activity. Other manufacturing held around the 100-point threshold separating expansion from contraction. The report identified energy shortages, inadequate raw-material supplies, high rental costs, tight credit conditions and infrastructure deficiencies as major constraints facing manufacturers. These challenges increased operating costs and discouraged fresh investment. In agriculture, the CBPI rose to 117.7 points in September from 110.5 points in August and 107.3 points a year earlier. Crop production and agro-allied activities recorded stronger expansion, while livestock activity slowed. Forestry and fishing moved into contraction. The sector nevertheless faced inadequate financing, power outages, insecurity and infrastructure bottlenecks. Meanwhile, services activity slowed, with its index declining to 107.7 points from 112.4 points in August, although it remained in expansion territory. The NESG’s findings indicate that stronger trade and agricultural activity supported the broader economy, even as mounting cost pressures and operational constraints continued to undermine manufacturing performance.
